summary: Elevated 5xx from short-lived keepalive mismatch causing gateway throttler amplification and upstream runtime churn
description: Issue summary: AxisHealth reported a sudden spike in 502/503 responses for their streaming and short-payload chat routes during a morning traffic ramp. Impact: degraded availability for several customer integrations (timeouts and failed requests), increased token cost due to retries; affected customer is on Dedicated. Environment: prod-us-east dedicated pool; recent gateway config sweep (small-payload keepalive/cull) rolled out to ~20% of hosts at 02:20 UTC. Observed behavior: rapid elevation in gateway 502/503s coincident with high short-connection rate; upstream serving-runtime processes experienced repeated soft restarts and GPU watch-dog evictions. Expected behavior: stable accept queues and graceful backpressure without runtime restarts. Key artifacts: heap and thread dumps from runtimes, apigw accept-queue histograms, throttler token burn charts, NVMe iowait graphs, connection churn traces. Next steps taken: immediate mitigation, live debugging, and permanent fixes documented below.
steps_to_reproduce: On a dedicated-us-east test shard, send repeated small streaming/openai-like chunks with keepalive=1s and client reconnects every 800ms to emulate churn
Run parallel short-payload embedding uploads to simulate mixed workload (embedding + chat) against the same tenant routing key
Observe apigw accept-queue depth, throttler tokens, and runtime process metrics (cpu, iowait, thread count) during the ramp
comments: 2026-03-13 02:30 - Support (Maya): Customer reported 502s for short streaming sessions starting ~02:20 UTC. Providing initial log bundle and asking for prioritization.

2026-03-13 02:45 - SRE (Aaron): Noted accept-queue growth on a subset of apigw hosts receiving the new keepalive cull config; throttler token burn anomalously high for small-payload flows. Spinning up debug instances and toggling rollout to 0% for affected hosts.
2026-03-13 03:05 - Customer (AxisHealth - Elaine Carter): Confirming large number of transient failures; some clients are aggressive on reconnect and seeing retries compounded.

2026-03-13 03:12 - Infra (Priya): Rolled back keepalive cull change for us-east canaries, increased accept-queue soft limit on apigw, and applied throttler soft cap fix. Early signal: error-rate dropping.
2026-03-14 09:00 - Post-incident (Aaron): Follow-up summary shared; mitigation validated and postmortem scheduled. Customer acceptance received and monitoring in steady state.
investigation_notes: Correlation: 02:20 UTC gateway config sweep for keepalive/cull coincident with error spike on ~10% of apigw hosts.
Hypothesis A: Keepalive cull reduced long-lived connection reuse; increased short connection churn created head-of-line pressure in accept queues leading to bursty hedged retries.
Hypothesis B: Throttler misaccounted token consumption for small payloads when combined with hedged client retry behavior, causing amplified ingress and backlog.
Runtime observation: Serving-runtimes showed NVMe background compaction jobs overlapping the spike -> iowait rose and GPU watchdogs evicted processes under CPU/io pressure.
Ticketed an infra change: throttler logic to better distinguish short-payload/streaming work (PR referenced below), and accept-queue backpressure tuning for small-fanout tenants.
Customer impact window estimated: 02:20–03:10 UTC; peak error-rate reached 12% on affected routes for AxisHealth tenant.
Related artifacts: heap-profiler snapshots and a trimmed tcpdump for one apigw host attached to PR; see related_github_prs and confluence link.
resolution: Mitigation: rolled back keepalive cull rollout on affected apigw hosts, applied throttler soft-cap patch to reduce token overcommit for short payloads, increased apigw accept-queue soft limit temporarily, and scheduled a delayed NVMe compaction window to avoid overlap with peak traffic. Result: 502/503 rate returned to baseline within ~18 minutes after rollback. Permanent fix: throttler patch merged + follow-up tuning and a postmortem with action items.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-13 03:12 UTC - rollback of keepalive cull to 0% for us-east canaries completed (Priya).

2026-03-14 - Permanent throttler PR merged into main: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4321 (schedules token accounting for short-payload flows).

Follow-up: postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-16; action items include add canary traffic shape tests for keepalive/cull, move NVMe compaction windows, and add tenant isolation for throttler accounting.
